review_note: Two independent Hom-exactness biconditionals match pinned source: contravariant Hom(-,N) characterizes right exactness M1→M2→M3→0; covariant Hom(N,-) characterizes left exactness 0→M1→M2→M3. Both universally quantify over N.
statement:
Exactness and $\Hom_R$. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$
be $R$-modules. Let $M_1 \to M_2$ and $M_2 \to M_3$ be $R$-module maps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3 \to 0$ is exact if and only if
$0 \to \Hom_R(M_3, N) \to \Hom_R(M_2, N) \to \Hom_R(M_1, N)$
is exact for all $R$-modules $N$.
\item $0 \to M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3$ is exact if and only if
$0 \to \Hom_R(N, M_1) \to \Hom_R(N, M_2) \to \Hom_R(N, M_3)$
is exact for all $R$-modules $N$.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-hom-exact}
Exactness and $\Hom_R$. Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$
be $R$-modules. Let $M_1 \to M_2$ and $M_2 \to M_3$ be $R$-module maps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3 \to 0$ is exact if and only if
$0 \to \Hom_R(M_3, N) \to \Hom_R(M_2, N) \to \Hom_R(M_1, N)$
is exact for all $R$-modules $N$.
\item $0 \to M_1 \to M_2 \to M_3$ is exact if and only if
$0 \to \Hom_R(N, M_1) \to \Hom_R(N, M_2) \to \Hom_R(N, M_3)$
is exact for all $R$-modules $N$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Preserves the finitely presented source-module requirement and both localized-Hom identities, one for f∈R and another for arbitrary multiplicative S. Includes Hom over both R and the localized ring, without reversing map direction.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R$-module.
Let $N$ be an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $f \in R$ we have
$\Hom_R(M, N)_f = \Hom_{R_f}(M_f, N_f) = \Hom_R(M_f, N_f)$,
\item for a multiplicative subset $S$ of $R$ we have
$$
S^{-1}\Hom_R(M, N) = \Hom_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N) =
\Hom_R(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N).
$$
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-hom-from-finitely-presented}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $R$-module.
Let $N$ be an $R$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $f \in R$ we have
$\Hom_R(M, N)_f = \Hom_{R_f}(M_f, N_f) = \Hom_R(M_f, N_f)$,
\item for a multiplicative subset $S$ of $R$ we have
$$
S^{-1}\Hom_R(M, N) = \Hom_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N) =
\Hom_R(S^{-1}M, S^{-1}N).
$$
\end{enumerate}
